title: Provider Exit Velocity Sentinel: predictive watchlist & disruption playbook
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Purpose: build a lightweight predictive system and operational watchlist that assigns a short-term 'exit velocity' score to model providers and hosted endpoints so product, SRE, and sales can pre-emptively act when a provider shows signs of imminent disruption. Motivation: customers care less about abstract vendor risk and more about interruption windows for production inference (latency spikes, sudden quota changes, regional unavailability). This ticket scopes the PM work to define signals, data sources, scoring model, priority watchlist UI, and an actionable disruption playbook for the Console and sales SREs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Signal taxonomy defined with at least 8 independent indicators (price delta, quantization release cadence, tail-latency spikes, region-level 5xx rate, reported SLAs changes, package deprecations, partner capacity allocations, downstream customer churn signals). 2) Prototype scoring function implemented in a reproducible notebook that ranks 150 providers by exit velocity. 3) A Console Watchlist mock and an associated alerting spec (thresholds, pager routing, escalation). 4) Playbook written with runbooks for three scenarios: transient latency storm, capacity embargo, and vendor sunset. 5) Stakeholder review and sign-off from SRE, Sales Ops, and Legal.
tasks: Collect telemetry and external signals: token price changes, public release notes, infra status pages, region latency histograms, support ticket count
Design scoring rubric and weight priors for signals (documented rationale)
Implement prototype pipeline in a Colab/Notebook (data ingestion + scoring)
Visual mockups for Console Watchlist (owner, score trend, top contributing signals)
Draft disruption playbook with automated fallback suggestions (model variants, region reroute, cached responses)
Run tabletop exercise with SRE and Sales for one high-value customer scenario
Prepare PRD and handoff to ENG for production telemetry pipeline and UI integration

notes: Design constraints: keep false positives low for P1 alerts. Scoring should emphasize velocity (recent change) over absolute risk to avoid flagging long-lived degraded providers incorrectly. We will iterate thresholds in a 4-week experimentation window. Consider privacy: only use public and internal telemetry; Legal requires review before using scraped forum posts. Quantitative targets: aim for >70% precision in retrospective (past 6 months) simulation for incidents defined as >30% sustained latency degradation for 3+ hours.
